key_insight: Encoder–decoder operator learning admits a resolution-independent theory because the induced kernels converge to a limiting kernel, letting approximation and generalization errors be analyzed without tying regularity assumptions to the discretization level.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a principled way to design and scale encoder–decoder models for PDEs and operator learning across different resolutions, with explicit error bounds and complexity guarantees.
method: Map matrix-valued kernels on encoded data to operator-valued kernels on the original function spaces via RKHS isomorphism.
Analyze limiting kernels through operator-norm convergence of the associated integral operators as input/output resolutions increase.
Derive upper and lower error bounds for regularized SGD and extend the framework to wide encoder–decoder networks via the limiting NTK.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical upper and lower bounds for regularized SGD and NTK-based encoder–decoder networks, including optimization terms of order t^{-θ} and T^{-θ'} and finite-width/error-complexity guarantees.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on encoding-induced approximation terms and finite-width effects, so practical performance can still degrade if the discretization or width is not sufficiently large.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
